summary: solidity-gas-watcher ships 4.3MB obfuscated loader auto-executed on require()
details: Package 'solidity-gas-watcher' is a disguised payload carrier. The package.json declares name 'solidity-gas-watcher' with a 'vulnerabilities management' description, but the tarball ships files from the unrelated pino logger project (lib/levels.js, lib/proto.js, lib/transport.js, docs/, pino README) as cover content. The declared main (index.js) is a stub Express-style middleware whose only material effect is `const config = require('./lib/config')`, which loads lib/config.js — a 4,373,384-byte single-line obfuscator.io bundle (string array of ~26,185 entries, hex-escaped identifiers, rotated string-array decoder). The payload executes automatically on `require('solidity-gas-watcher')` with no caller action required. The package also declares axios as a runtime dependency, yet no readable source file references it, indicating the HTTP client is reserved for the obfuscated code. The combination of name/content/description mismatch, pino library files used as cover, a stub entry point, a multi-megabyte opaque loader auto-invoked on import, and an unused network-client dependency is the standard shape of an installer-targeting stealer rather than any legitimate functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
